title: Mariner 4 Mars Flyby (First Close-up Photos)
description: Mariner 4 executed the first successful planetary flyby of Mars, returning 21 iconic close-up pictures showing impact craters.

title: Surveyor 1 Lunar Soft Landing
description: Surveyor 1 proved spacecraft could touch down softly on the Moon without sinking into deep dust, clearing the way for Apollo.

title: Lunar Orbiter 1 Controlled Impact
description: After photographing potential Apollo landing sites and capturing the historic Earthrise image, the orbiter was intentionally deorbited.

title: Apollo 11 'The Eagle Has Landed'
description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin set the Lunar Module Eagle down in Mare Tranquillitatis. The descent stage remains in place today.

title: First Extraterrestrial Vehicle Drive (Apollo 15 LRV)
description: Astronauts David Scott and James Irwin drove the first Lunar Roving Vehicle 27.8 km along the deep gorge of Hadley Rille.

title: Viking 1 Lander Touches Down on Mars
description: First successful US landing on Mars. Returned the first color photographs from the surface of another planet.

title: Viking 2 Touchdown at Utopia Planitia
description: Viking 2 touches down on Utopia Planitia, analyzing soil samples and monitoring Martian weather for over 3 Martian years.

title: Viking 1 Communications Cease
description: A software uplink accidentally overwrote antenna pointing instructions, concluding 6 years of continuous surface science.

title: Mars Pathfinder Airbag Landing in Ares Vallis
description: Pathfinder bounces to a stop encased in airbags and deploys the Sojourner microrover onto the ancient flood channel.

title: Sojourner Rover Rollout
description: Sojourner becomes the first autonomous mobile rover on Mars, analyzing chemical compositions of rocks Barnacle Bill and Yogi.

title: 2001 Mars Odyssey Orbit Insertion
description: Mars Odyssey arrives at Mars and begins aerobraking, eventually discovering vast reservoirs of shallow sub-surface water ice.

title: Spirit Rover Airbag Touchdown in Gusev Crater
description: Spirit lands inside the 160-km wide Gusev Crater to search for evidence of ancient lake sedimentation.

title: Opportunity Lands 'Hole in One' in Eagle Crater
description: Opportunity rolls into Eagle Crater and immediately discovers layered bedrock and hematite spherules ('blueberries').

title: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) Arrives
description: MRO enters Martian orbit and begins high-resolution surface mapping with its 0.5-meter HiRISE camera telescope.

title: Phoenix Lander Verifies Subsurface Water Ice
description: Phoenix robotic scoop exposed dice-sized bright white clumps in trench 'Dodo-Goldilocks' that vaporized over 4 days, proving pure water ice.

title: LRO Launch & Lunar Mapping
description: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter launches to map the Moon's 3D topography and pinpoint ancient equipment remains.

title: Spirit Rover Sends Final Transmission
description: Trapped in soft sand at site 'Troy', Spirit entered low-power hibernation during the cold southern Martian winter and never woke.

title: Curiosity Sky Crane Touchdown in Gale Crater
description: NASA successfully executes the revolutionary Sky Crane maneuver, gently lowering the 899-kg Curiosity rover onto Mars.

title: Curiosity Confirms Ancient Habitable Lake
description: Drill powder from mudstone at Yellowknife Bay revealed sulfur, nitrogen, hydrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and carbon—the building blocks for life.

title: Opportunity Rover Sends Final Transmission
description: A catastrophic planet-encircling dust storm blotted out the Sun in Perseverance Valley, depleting Opportunity's solar battery power.

title: Perseverance Lands in Jezero Crater
description: Perseverance touches down using Terrain-Relative Navigation in an ancient delta bed to search for fossilized microbial life.

title: Ingenuity Achieves First Powered Atmospheric Flight
description: Ingenuity lifts 3 meters above Wright Brothers Field on Mars, proving aerodynamic flight is feasible in Mars' thin 1% atmosphere.

title: InSight Lander Retired in Elysium Planitia
description: After four years and recording over 1,300 marsquakes, InSight's solar panels become completely smothered in red dust.

title: Ingenuity Concludes Historic 72-Flight Mission
description: After damaging a carbon-fiber rotor blade on landing during Flight 72, Ingenuity officially retires at Valinor Hills.

title: Perseverance Surpasses 45.2 km Driving Distance
description: NASA telemetry records Perseverance driving 45.22 km, surpassing Opportunity's 14-year endurance record across Martian soil.
